title: Define compat-level taxonomy and soft-pin semantics for community model intake
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Clarify requirements and acceptance criteria for how community/third-party open models are labeled in the catalog (compatibility taxonomy) and how 'soft-pins' should behave at runtime. This PRD fragment resolves ambiguity from previous onboarding tickets about fallback semantics, auto-unpin triggers, and the minimum runtime checks required before a variant is allowed to receive production traffic.
goals: Create a small, actionable "compat-level" taxonomy designers and engineers can apply during intake.
Define soft-pin semantics: what pinning means, how long pins last, and how fallback chains are constructed and enforced at runtime.
Specify automated runtime sanity checks and minimum eval signal thresholds required to graduate an open model to 'serving-allowed' status.
Provide a staged rollout plan with monitoring and fallback for new catalog entries to avoid reliability regressions.
requirements: Each catalog entry for a community model must include compat_level (one of: 'native', 'adapter', 'soft-unsupported', 'blocked') and a reason string.
The catalog UI/API must expose 'soft_pin' metadata: default_variant, pin_timestamp, author, and optional expiry_date.
Runtime must honor a per-customer fallback chain: requested_variant -> pinned_variant -> runtime-default-compatible-variant -> explicit-block error.
Soft-pins are advisory by default: serving runtime can fall back when latency/SLO breaches are detected; hard pins (enterprise customers) require explicit opt-in and override fallback behavior.

Automated onboarding checks: model passes a lightweight runtime smoke test (end-to-end generation for 3 prompt shapes), tokenization sanity, and quantization compatibility flags. These checks must run in a sandboxed canary environment before catalog entry becomes 'canary-eligible'.

Quality gate: new open model must pass a regression eval on the team's canonical prompt set with no more than 10% negative delta on defined metrics vs. a baseline variant, or be flagged for manual review.
Compatibility notes must enumerate required runtime features (KV cache, rotary/ALiBi parity, required kernel path), and recommended quantization profile.
out_of_scope: Full evaluator pipeline upgrades — this ticket only defines acceptance criteria and metadata, not the eval infra implementation.
Automated conversion/adaptation tooling (e.g., automatic tokenizer patching).
Billing and pricing changes related to pin/fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: API: New catalog intake endpoint accepts compat_level and soft_pin fields and persists them; documented in the catalog API spec.
Console: Model detail page renders compat_level badge and soft_pin metadata with tooltip explaining runtime semantics.
Runtime: In a canary run, a model marked 'adapter' or 'native' must successfully complete 3 smoke-generation tasks without KV-cache crashes; test logs are captured.

Fallback: When a pinned variant is intentionally throttled in the canary, runtime must transparently route to the next compatible variant in the chain and surface a trace in the console (trace shows pin->fallback decision).
Regression signal: A synthetic regression check against the canonical prompt set runs for the canary population and produces a pass/fail; pass must be recorded before broad rollout.
Documentation: Short PRD update and onboarding checklist added to Confluence with example compat_level annotations and a sample soft_pin lifecycle.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (Design): Finalize compat-level definitions and pin semantics with Eng and Design (this ticket).
Stage 1 (Canary): Allow model entries with compat_level in catalog but only route 0.5-2% of non-production traffic; run runtime smoke tests and regression checks for 48h.
Stage 2 (Limited Beta): If canary passes, expand to 10% of traffic for a week with close monitoring; enable automated fallback traces and SLO alerts.
Stage 3 (General Availability): After 1 week of stable telem and no critical incidents, mark model as GA and remove advisory restrictions.
decisions: Adopt a small, discrete compat_level taxonomy instead of free-text compatibility notes to make routing deterministic.
Soft-pins will be advisory by default; enterprise customers can request hard pins that change runtime fallback behavior (separate flow).
Compatibility checks will be lightweight smoke tests integrated into the intake pipeline; full evals remain a separate gating step.
open_questions: Should the compat_level be mutable after initial intake, and if so, what approval flow is required? (proposal: allow annotation updates with audit trail and 2 reviewer approvals).
What exact metrics define 'negative delta' for regression checks (accuracy/F1/ROUGE/LL/perplexity)? Need engineering guidance on compute cost tradeoffs.
How should we surface fallback events to downstream customers (webhook, console banner, or both)?
Do we permit auto-expiry of soft-pins after a configurable TTL (e.g., 90 days) to avoid stale pins?
